e: From Middle English *eking, *eching, deverbal of eken (“to increase, add”), equivalent to eke + -ing. More at eke.
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

q: Kenyan runners were highly sought after to anchor teams that competed in the Japanese distance relay, known as ekiden, in which 10 runners often combine to cover more than 200 kilometers.
2009 April 25, Joshua Robinson, “Olympic Champion Leads New Wave of Marathoners”, in New York Times:

e: Borrowed from Japanese 駅弁(えきべん) (ekiben).
From Ancient Greek οἰκίστικα (oikístika), from οἰκιστής (oikistḗs, “colonizer”). Coined by Constantinos Apostolou Doxiadis in 1942.
